variants.headline: Looking back: accident at a workplace
variants.sub: The workplace {facility} has had an accident.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: An accident had occurred at {facility}.

An accident at work. A plain statement, and a reason to remember that a workplace is full of people rather than merely output. No lurid description is needed. Readers deserve attention to safety without being sold an injury, a culprit or a scene that this report does not establish.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We criticise {target} on the standard of safety stewardship. An accident warrants serious questions about responsibility, rather than a comfortable presumption that the conduct surrounding work should remain beyond public judgment.

variants.headline: Looking back: workplace safety becomes immediate news
variants.sub: There has been an accident at {facility}.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: The workplace {facility} had had an accident.

An accident at work. A plain statement, and a reason to remember that a workplace is full of people rather than merely output. No lurid description is needed. Readers deserve attention to safety without being sold an injury, a culprit or a scene that this report does not establish.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We criticise {target} on the standard of safety stewardship. An accident warrants serious questions about responsibility, rather than a comfortable presumption that the conduct surrounding work should remain beyond public judgment.

variants.headline: Looking back: an accident enters the working day
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: There had been an accident at {facility}.

An accident at work. A plain statement, and a reason to remember that a workplace is full of people rather than merely output. No lurid description is needed. Readers deserve attention to safety without being sold an injury, a culprit or a scene that this report does not establish.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We criticise {target} on the standard of safety stewardship. An accident warrants serious questions about responsibility, rather than a comfortable presumption that the conduct surrounding work should remain beyond public judgment.
